intro.title: Generic List<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable list component that can display any type of data, such as a list of names, numbers, or custom objects. You will learn how to use TypeScript generics, specifically the Generic List<T> pattern, to create flexible and type-safe components in React. The main technologies involved are React functional components, JSX for rendering, and TypeScript's generic type parameters. By the end, you will understand how to write a single component that works with multiple data types while ensuring your code is robust and easy to maintain.
intro.usecase: Generic List<T> patterns appear in nearly every React application that displays dynamic data collections. You'll use them when building product catalogs with filterable item grids, user dashboards with sortable data tables, or social media feeds that render different post types. This approach allows developers to create reusable components that can display any type of data while maintaining type safety and reducing code duplication. For example, a single <GenericList> component could render employee directories, project task lists, or e-commerce product cards without rewriting display logic for each data type.
